name: Conjonctyl

card.summary: A mesotherapy injection product tested in a trial for body contouring, aimed at reducing circumference in treated areas.
card.note: Injectable procedure product; a single trial compared it with other mixtures.

quick.overview:
Conjonctyl is a branded mixture used in mesotherapy, a technique of small injections into the skin of areas where people want less fat. It was one of three lipolytic combinations compared in a randomized trial.

Its looks payoff is body contouring: reduced circumference in treated sites. In the 2011 trial of 75 women, the Conjonctyl group averaged 2.10 cm circumference loss per site.
quick.how: In the trial it was given as weekly mesotherapy injections over 15 treatments by clinicians. No self-administration guidance applies.
quick.risks: The trial reported no irregularities, dimples or serious side effects. Mesotherapy products vary and regulatory status differs by country.

lead: Conjonctyl is a product used in cosmetic mesotherapy, the practice of injecting small amounts of active mixtures into the skin to reduce local fat.[1]

A randomized trial of 75 women (mean age 33) compared three mixtures: phosphatidylcholine/deoxycholic acid, caffeine, and Conjonctyl, each given weekly for 15 treatments.[1] Average circumference reductions per site were 4.41 cm, 2.99 cm and 2.10 cm respectively, and 98.7% showed a body-fat percentage decrease.[1]

chain: Smaller circumference of the treated area
angle.text: Mesotherapy products like this are used with the aim of slimming treated areas, such as thighs or abdomen. The trial measured weight, body fat percentage and circumference.

paras: The 2011 trial randomized 75 women into three groups and measured weight, body fat percentage, circumference and satisfaction.[1] Ninety-six percent had circumference loss; the Conjonctyl group lost 2.10 cm per site and 2.82 kg of weight on average, versus larger changes in the phosphatidylcholine group.[1] Patient satisfaction was 63%, and no serious side effects or irregularities were reported.[1]

timeline.event: Randomized trial comparing three mesotherapy mixtures published.[1]
